headline: Carbon removal and CCUS enter COP31 cover-decision talks
summary: CDR and CCUS officially entered preliminary discussions for the COP31 cover decision after an informal consultation summary released by the Turkiye Presidency on 13 Nov; whether the language survives depends on later drafting rounds.
co2crc_note: Explicit CCUS/CDR text in a COP cover decision would legitimise CCS in the UNFCCC process and shape national policy signals Australia tracks.

headline: Mining waste touted at COP31 as a goldmine for scaling carbon removal
summary: A COP31 session framed mine tailings and alkaline mining waste as a large, under-used feedstock for enhanced rock weathering and mineralisation-based CO2 removal, arguing it could help scale durable CDR cheaply.
co2crc_note: Mineralisation/enhanced weathering pathways are adjacent to CO2CRC's geological-storage focus and relevant to Australia's large mining-waste streams.

headline: Gulf carbon-capture outlook cut as hydrogen projects stall
summary: Analysis reports the Gulf's carbon-capture deployment outlook has been slashed as blue-hydrogen projects that would anchor CO2 capture stall on weak offtake demand, dampening near-term CCS build-out expectations across the region.
co2crc_note: Gulf NOC CCS pipelines are a global benchmark; a slowdown reshapes competitive supply of storage capacity and blue-product markets Australia also eyes.

headline: Occidental targets ~4 Mtpa CO2 supply via new carbon-capture partnerships
summary: Occidental said it is targeting around 4 million tonnes per year of CO2 supply through new carbon-capture partnerships, building on CO2 offtake deals flagged at its Q3 results and feeding its Permian CO2-EOR and 1PointFive DAC strategy.
co2crc_note: Quantifies Oxy's CO2-supply ambition; CO2-EOR-linked offtake remains a template and a credibility question for CCS business models.

headline: COP31 panel warns buyers to lock in carbon-removal supply before demand surges
summary: A COP31 panel warned companies to secure durable carbon-removal supply now, before anticipated demand outstrips a still-thin supply of high-quality CDR credits and pushes prices up.
co2crc_note: CDR market-tightness signals underpin the longer-term revenue case for engineered carbon storage.

headline: Analysis: Pathways CCS economics hinge on government support
summary: An analysis of the Pathways Alliance oil-sands CCS project argues its underlying economics do not work without substantial federal and Alberta government support, framing the live fiscal-agreement negotiations as decisive for FID.
co2crc_note: Pathways is a bellwether for public-support dependence of large CCS; its economics debate informs Australia's own funding-gap discussion.

headline: Community pushback and regulatory uncertainty give pause in the CCS space
summary: A US trade-press piece reports that community opposition and regulatory uncertainty are causing developers to hesitate on CCS projects, underscoring the social-licence and permitting risks around pipelines and storage siting.
co2crc_note: Social-licence friction and permitting delay are the same headwinds CO2CRC-adjacent projects face in winning community acceptance.
